newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco grants leftist group legal status.
newsitem.headline: Morocco grants leftist group legal status.

text.p: Morocco's interior ministry said on Wednesday it had given authority for a group of dissident left-wing politicians to form a new political party.
The new movement, called the Democratic Socialist Party (DSP), was set up by politicians who broke with the well-established leftist Organisation of Democratic and Popular Action (OADP).
The DSP held its first meeting and appointed university professor Issa El-Ouardighi, 48, as secretary general last week, a spokesman for the interior ministry said.
"We consider ourselves as a part of the left movement and of the opposition al-Koutla Addimokratia (democratic bloc)," Ourdighi was quoted by local press as saying.
Al-Koutla Addimokratia, which was set up in the early 1990s, was formed of the old-guard Istiqlal party, the Socialist Union of People's Forces, the Progress and Socialist Party and the OADP.
The group broke from the OADP after a dispute between members of the leadership over the participation in the referendum on constitutional reform last September.
According to official figures, 99.56 percent, or 10.16 million people voted "yes" in the referendum which took place on September 13.
Members of the DSP opposed the OADP leadership's call for a boycott of the referendum.
Morocco has 12 active parties of which six are in the opposition. Two groups with Islamic leanings have campaigned for the last decade for legal status but with no result.
